newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND MULLS REGIONAL INITIATIVE OVER BELARUS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND MULLS REGIONAL INITIATIVE OVER BELARUS.

text.p: Poland, anxious over events in Belarus, on Tuesday hastily prepared initiatives to support democracy and sovereignty in the neighbouring state where President Alexander Lukashenko was clashing with parliament.
Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski said Warsaw was sounding out Ukraine and Lithuania on a possible joint statement by the three presidents.

"We cannot regard what is going on in Belarus on the basis of saying 'it's not happening in our house and it's none of our business'," PAP news agency quoted Kwasniewski as saying after meeting the prime, foreign, defence and interior ministers.

He said the proposed statement would say that Belarus sovereignty was in Europe's interests and the three countries were ready to support everything that served democracy, the rule of law and the economic development of Belarus.

Kwasniewski's spokesman Antoni Styrczula told Reuters the president had repeatedly written to Lukashenko, saying that democratic reforms in Belarus should continue and that human rights and media freedoms should be respected.
The strongly pro-Russian Lukashenko, defying parliament and the constitutional court, has called a referendum on Sunday in a bid to increase his powers and extend his term by two years.
Critics accuse him of dictatorial tendencies.

The Belarus issue was high on the agenda of a Warsaw cabinet meeting on Tuesday, where Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati was due to report on developments in the former Soviet state of 10 million people.

Before the meeting, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said Belarus events were causing deep unease although he hoped that the situation there could still be resolved according to the principles of democracy and the rule of law.
"We would be very worried and disturbed if that was not the case," Cimoszewicz told reporters.

Poland hopes to join NATO soon, a goal strongly opposed by Lukashenko who echoes Russian arguments that the western defence alliance's eastward expansion could pose a threat to the former Soviet states.
Warsaw politicians fear that political and economic instability in Belarus could complicate its NATO entry plans and harm its economic interests.

The Polish parliament's foreign affairs committee proposed a resolution on Belarus. The draft says it is unacceptable to break democratic rules, which would menace the internal stability and sovereignty of Belarus, infringe its constitution and human rights, threaten dictatorship and remove it from the sphere of democratic European countries.
The lower house may vote on the draft on Wednesday.
